So the master said to the servant, ‘Go out to the country roads and lanes and make people come in, so that my house will be full. I tell you all that none of those men who were invited will taste my dinner’.  (Luke 14:16-24).
meditation: In this parable, the owner of the feast is God, feast is God’s call in heaven. People attached to worldly affairs are telling excuses when God calls us to enjoy with him in heaven. The first one has already purchased the field. Has he purchased it without seeing it in advance? The second one has already purchased the five pairs of oxen. Has he purchased without seeing them before purchase? Though married to a woman, the third one can enjoy the feast along with his wife.

All those excuses do not hold any water. We can assume that the invited people may be  the chosen people of Israelites or those gentiles who believed in faith in God and called on to be his sons by his grace. Any of us who are blessed by him and do not live as per his wish and are involved in worldly affairs, we are bound to lose heaven permanently as well as the honor and privilege  of God’s calling.
Carelessness of the invited for salvation - God’s grace to the gentiles for eternity.
parables.prayer: Our heavenly Father, thank you for your grace to provide eternity to all the generations on earth including gentiles. Help us to be attentive at your  call for salvation of our spirits.  We pray in the name of Jesus Christ.  Amen.

parables.title: Parable on the cost of being a Disciple.
scripture: “Once when large crowds of people  were going along with Jesus, he turned and said to them, ‘Whoever comes to me can not be my disciple unless he loves me  more than he loves his father and mother, his wife and his children,  his brothers and his sisters, and himself as well. Whoever does not carry his own cross and come after me cannot be my disciple.’

‘If one of you is planning to build a tower, he sits down first and worksout what it will cost, to see if he has  enough money to finish the job. If he doesn’t, he will not be able to finish the tower after laying the foundation; and all who see what happened will laugh at him. This man began to build but cannot finish the job’, they will say.

If a king goes out with ten thousand men to fight another king who comes against with twenty thousand men, he will sit down first and decide if he is strong enough to face that other king. If he isn’t, he will send messengers to meet the other king, to ask for terms of peace while he is still a long way off. ‘In the same way’, concluded Jesus, ‘none of you can be my disciple unless he gives up everything he has’.” (Luke 14:25-35).
meditation: We have to understand the inner meaning of the words of Jesus ‘to leave father, mother, wife, children and even one self, if one wants to really be a disciple of Jesus. It doesn’t mean to reject  the family relations, without a reason which He has given us to dwell and enjoy.

If it is a call to follow Jesus as a disciple, he should be prepared to leave everything including his family and self. The disciples of Jesus, Apostle the Paul, Stephen and many more are prepared to die for Jesus. And they all created their history for Jesus, and God was glorified.

In those days, many followed Jesus to see the miracles, to see the healings and also to hear his teachings. Some people followed to get healings, some to get on their day of bread, and some to find faults with Jesus. Jesus knows all their minds. Following does not mean to simply go wherever he goes. It means to follow His commandments truly and faithfully.

In this parable, Jesus advised all to do any work after planning and assessing truly about the ins and outs of the work they wanted to do with truth and faith. Jesus said in Luke 9:62,  ‘Any one who starts to plough and then keeps looking back is of no use to the kingdom of God’.

Jesus wanted everybody to lead a life useful to people and to the glory of God. He compared our life as salt, since if it loses saltiness it becomes useless for men, and useless to earth even as manure also. He wanted everybody to introspect themselves and rectify.

“Love thy Lord with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind” and ‘Love your neighbor as  you love yourself’, said Jesus. If we cannot love our neighbor we cannot love Jesus. Loving Jesus means to follow Jesus and live according to his teachings.

In the old testament, Shedreck, Mehek and Abednego are prepared to be thrown into fire. They did not care about anything, including their high official possessions and honor except praying to God. They expressed candidly before the king that they do not bow down before any idol, which is against the command of God. They are prepared to die even if  God does not save them from burning in fire.

After crucifixion and death and after the resurrection of Jesus, the disciples are prepared to spread the good news to everybody, and they are prepared to face any persecutions and troubles and become christian martyrs.

Those who want to follow Jesus should confirm themselves to face any challenge. Otherwise, we become a laughing stock before the worldly people and  Satan. Such a situation is not for the glory of God, and we should not bring such undesirable situation  to the name of God.
Those who want to be a Disciple of Christ should be prepared to leave everything and prepared to face any consequence.
parables.prayer: Our heavenly Father, we understand that we can be disciples and glorify you, putting all our efforts, if necessary by ignoring all our worldly comforts including family and self.  Help us to follow you wholeheartedly and glorify you.  We pray in the name of Jesus Christ.  Amen.

parables.title: Parable on the lost son
scripture: Before telling the parable on ‘The Lost son’, Jesus told two more parables. “Suppose one of you has a hundred sheep and loses one of them - what does he do? He leaves the other ninety-nine sheep in the pasture and goes looking for the one that got lost until he finds it.

When he finds it,  he is so happy that he puts it on his shoulders and carries it back home. Then he calls his friends and neighbors together and says to them, ‘I am so happy, I found my lost sheep. Let us celebrate’.

Similarly a woman who has ten silver coins loses one of them, what does she do? She lights a lamp, sweeps her house, and looks carefully everywhere until she finds it.  When she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors together and says to them, ‘I am so happy I found the coin I lost. Let us celebrate’.
In the same way I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner, who repents than over ninety-nine respecting people who do not need to repent. (Luke 15:1-10).

This is the parable on the lost son. “There was once a man who had two sons. The younger one said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of property right now’. So the man divided his property between his two sons. After a few days, the younger son sold his part of the property and left home with the money.

He went to a country far away, and wasted his money in reckless living. He spent everything he had. Then a severe famine spread over that country, and he left without a thing. So he went to work for one of the citizens of that country, who sent him out to his farm to take care of the pigs. He wished he could fill himself with the bean pods the pigs ate.  but no one gave him anything to eat.

At last he came to his senses and said, ‘All my father’s hired workers have more than they can eat, and here I am about to  starve. I will get up and go to my father and say, ‘Father, I have sinned against God and against you. I am no longer fit to be called your son; treat me as one of your hired workers’. So he got up and started back to his father.

He was still a long way from home when his father  saw him, his heart was filled with pity, and he ran, threw his arms around his son, and kissed him. “Father”, the son said, ‘I have sinned against God and against you, I am no longer fit to be called  your son’.

But the father called his servants, ‘Hurry’, he said, ‘Bring the best rob and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and shoes on his feet, then go and get the  prize calf and kill it, and let us celebrate with a feast. For this son of mine was dead, but now he is alive, he was lost, but  now he has been found’, and so the feasting began. (Luke 15:11-32).

In the meantime the elder son was  out in the field. On his way back, when he came close to the house, he heard music and dancing. So he called one of his servants and asked him, ‘What’s going on’. ‘Your brother has come back home’, the servant answered, ‘and your father has killed the prize calf, because he got him back, safe and sound’.

The elder brother was so angry that he would not go into the house; so his father came out and begged him to come in. But he answered his father, look, all these years I have worked for you like a slave, and I have never disobeyed your orders. What have you given to me? Not even a goat for me to have a feast with my friends.

But this son of yours wasted all your property on prostitutes, and when he comes back home, you killed the prize calf for him’. ‘My son’, the father answered, ‘you are always here with me, and everything I have is yours. But we had to celebrate and be happy, because your brother was dead, but now he is alive; he was lost, but now he has been found’.”

Many tax collectors and sinners are coming to hear Jesus. Pharisees and the teachers of the Law did not like Jesus to be with the sinners and participating taking food with them. It is because Jesus came from Judas, the Pharisees and teachers of Law did not like Jesus to participate, taking food with them and speaking with the sinners, because they are all treated as low caste people and gentiles who are looked down upon by the Judas.

The younger son is compared as a sinner with worldly attractions, departed from his father, encashed all the property he got in his name and left to a far off place,  spent it for bad habits and finally left with nothing. We are learning here that self wisdom and bad habits lead a man to lose everything and leave with nothing.

All humans are the sons of God. Worldly attractions and our wrong ways, keeps us away from God and creates distance from God. But God is love. God loves us so much,  in spite of the fact that we want to get separated from him and misuse his gifts, our body, health and all other blessings.
meditation: Worldly people do not care for the starvation and the needs of a fellow person. The owner of the pigs behaved like that only. The starvation of the second son made him realize his faults and crave for the love of his father (God). When he started to realize and started to come back, it made his father,  to long for his lost son. The honesty in his realization brought him back to his father, without any blame but in full honor.

Jesus said in Mathews 9:13 stating, “I have not come to call respectable people, but outcasts''. Jesus knows our heart. He came to provide salvation to the sinners. If we want to turn to God, he himself initiates to clean our sins and fill us with the Holy Spirit, heal us and bless us, as said in the parable.

Thinking that God saves us because he loves us so much, and if we do not confess our sins and leave them, and do not express ourself before God to save us, it is not possible to get blessings from God. If the second son, knowing that his father is very generous, did not express his faults, he may not have got love and affection of this range from his father.

The father tried to convince his family members (represented by his elder son), on the coming back of his second son. The Holy Spirit deputed by Jesus, is trying to convince God on behalf of us,  who are lost in the worldly attractions.

The eldest son became jealous. How long we may be in the fold of God’s love, Satan will always try to put us in temptations and jealousy, it will make use of every opportunity to keep us at a distance from God. The Holy Spirit in us  understands that bad situation and warns us to rectify.

The father in this parable tried to make the first son realize the situation and invited him to join the feast. So much so, we are to realize the bad situations in us at the time of temptations and rectify ourselves. We should leave jealousy, which is sin.

Repentance is the first attempt to leave sin. Since God knows our inner feelings in our heart, at that stage he will strengthen our good attempt. That is why, it is said that ‘God is striking at the door of our heart’, several ways. (see Revelation 3:20).

We may consider that the eldest son represents a normal christian in our society. We may be living like a good christian following God’s commandments. We may get jealous if God shows special attention to a person (who was a sinner, but later repented for his sins),  and we get jealous of that  repented person.
The father in this parable said to his eldest son, “You are always with me my son, and everything of mine is yours”. This assurance is much greater than a special attention God paid to the lost son.

True Christians can understand the value of the greater blessing. We are to learn from the character of the eldest son, that we are to live a faithful and satisfactory life with the God given talents.

The second son is lost on account of worldly attractions, but after repentance he gained his lost glory. It is left to our imagination whether  the first son who lived as a beloved son always attached to his father, seems to have lost his blessing on account of jealousy or rectified himself and joined the feast or not.

The father (God) in such critical situations tries to help his beloved sons (those named after him) in any manner, to realize and rectify and come back to Him. It is in our hands only to realize and rectify ourselves and come back to God’s fold. As told in the other parables of ‘Lost sheep’ and the ‘Lost coin’, it is confirmed that God’s wish is not to lose anyone from his hold.
Repentance of past sins and wrong thoughts and prayer for salvation, entails us for God’s grace.
parables.prayer: Our gracious Father, thank you for the love and longing for our comeback to your fold, from the worldly temptations. We also understand how we lose our blessed life comparing ourselves with our fellowmen. Help us to be always in your looks, which blessing is more valuable than anything in this world.  We pray in the name of Jesus Christ.  Amen.

parables.title: Parable on the Shrewd Manager
scripture: “There was once a rich man who had a servant who managed his property. The rich man was told that the manager was wasting his master's money, so he called in and said, ‘What is this I hear about you? Hand in a complete account of your handling of my property, because you cannot be my manager any longer.’

The servant said to himself, ‘My master is going to dismiss me from my job, what shall I do?.  I am not strong enough to dig ditches, and I am ashamed to beg. Now I will know what I will do! Then, when my job is gone I shall have friends who will welcome me in their homes’.

“So he called in all the people who were in debt to his master. He asked the first one, ‘How much do you owe my master? ‘One hundred barrels of olive oil,’  he answered. ‘Here is your account’, the manager told him, ‘sit down and write fifty’. Then he asked another one, ‘And you’ -- How much do you owe? ‘A thousand sacks of wheat,’ he answered. ‘Here is your account,’ the manager told him, 'write eight hundred’.

As a result, the master of this dishonest manager wondered of him for doing such a shrewd thing; because the people of this world are much more shrewd in handling their affairs than the people who belong to the light ie., honest people.

And Jesus went on to say, ‘And so I tell you; make friends for yourselves for worldly wealth, so that, when it gives out, you will be welcomed in the eternal home.’  “Whoever is faithful in small matters will be faithful in large ones; whoever is dishonest in small matters will be dishonest in large ones”.

If then, you have not been faithful in handling worldly wealth, how can you be trusted with true wealth? And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to someone else, who will give you what belongs to you? No servant can be the slave of two masters; he will hate one and love the other: he will be loyal to one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.” (Luke 16:1-13).
meditation: We are like the managers on this earth. Wealth, work and power are given to us by God. If the manager belongs to earth, he believes in Wealth. If he belongs to God, he believes in God. If the manager keeps his faith  on wealth, he cannot be faithful to the wealth entrusted to him, he tries to earn  some more money by unfaithful deeds towards his master and makes wrong and false promises to those worldly people and attracts them.

They will be showing shrewdness in their works. But they will lose faith even among the worldly people in due course of time. It is against God, if anybody shows unfaithfulness in small things or in  big things. God is questioning that if any one is not faithful even in small things on earth, who believes such persons in heaven.

Nothing in this world is ours, but everything is given by God. If we are not honest in what is entrusted by God to us in this world, even in small things,  how God believes us, though we pray for bigger and greater blessings. We are to learn here that we should be honest and faithful in all things entrusted by God to us, and live faithfully.

In Exodus 20:17, God commanded, “Do not desire another man’s house, do not desire his wife,  his slaves, his cattle, his donkeys, or anything else  that he owns”. If anybody really loves his neighbor, he will not desire anything that belongs to his neighbor. Wealth does not mean monetary blessing alone, but includes health, blessings and opportunities etc., also.
If we are dishonest with the talents given by God, how can we get more talents from God?
parables.prayer: Our heavenly Father, health, talents and gifts, blessings and opportunities, all are from you only. Help us to be honest in everything we are given.  We pray in the name of Jesus Christ.  Amen.

parables.title: Parable on the richman and the poor Lazar
scripture: “There was once a rich man who dressed in the most expensive clothes and lived in great luxury every day. There was also a poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores who used to be brought to the rich man’s door, hoping to eat the bits of food that fell from the richman’s table. Even the dogs come and lick his sores.

The poor man died and was carried by the angels to sit beside Abraham at the feast in heaven. The rich man died and he was buried, and in  Hades, where he was in great pain, he looked up and saw Abraham, far away, with Lazarous at his side. So he called out, ‘Father Abraham! take pity on me and send Lazarous to dip his finger in some water and cool my tongue, because I am in great pain in this fire.

But Abraham said, ‘Remember my son, that in your lifetime you were given all the good things, while Lazarous got all bad things. But now, he is enjoying himself here, while you are in pain. Besides all that, there is a deep pit lying between us, so that those who want to cross over from here to you cannot do so,  nor can anyone cross over to us from where you are.

The rich man said, then I beg you, father Abraham,  send Lazarous to my father’s house, where I have five brothers. Let him go and warn them so that they, at least, will not come to this place of pain’.

Abraham said, ‘Your brothers have Moses and the prophets to warn them; your brothers should listen to what they say’. The richman answered, ‘That is not enough, father Abraham, But if someone would rise from death and go to them, then they would turn from their sons.’ But Abraham said, ‘If they will not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be convinced even if someone  were to rise from death’. (Luke 16:19-31).
meditation: Rich or poor on earth are alike in the sight of God. It is difficult for the rich man to live on earth pleasing God. Jesus said to his disciples in Mathews 19:23 and in Mark 10:23, “I assure you; it will be very hard for rich people to enter the kingdom of God than for a camel to go through the eye of a needle”.

It is difficult for a man blessed with richness to be faithful in what he was given, because he loves richness and neglects God. It doesn’t mean that it is not possible for those to keep faith in God. There is nothing impossible to God.

Job, the richest man, was blessed like anything. His faith and dependence on God made him righteous by God and he was blessed double fold after facing troubles. Though poor, because of his attitude and humbleness Lazarous was treated as righteous and had the honor of sitting beside Abraham, the father of faith.

After death on earth, and on the last day of the universe, all were to be sent either to Heaven or Hell. There is no chance or probability to move from Heaven to Hell or vice versa, because there was a deep pit lying in between them. What ever possibility is to leave sins and repent and live according to the guidelines of prophets and live as per the commandments of God, while living on earth itself. It is the main lesson in this parable.

Jesus said that the people who do not hear the prophets naturally do not hear even if one raises after death. Jesus prophetically said this word in this parable   telling that he will have to die and rise from death.
According to the righteousness of the dead, they will be taken either to Heaven or to Hell. No use of repentance after death on earth.
parables.prayer: Our eternal Father, thank you Father for teaching that according to the righteousness of the dead, one can go to heaven or hell, and there is no use of repentance after death. Help us to be righteous and give us a mind to introspect ourselves every time and rectify.  We pray in the name of Jesus Christ.  Amen.

parables.title: A servant’s duty
scripture: Jesus said, “Suppose one of you has a servant, who is plowing or looking after the sheep.  When he comes in from the field, do you tell him to hurry and eat his meal? Of course not. Instead, you say to him ‘Get my supper ready, then put on your apron,  and wait on me, while  I eat and drink, after that you may have your meal’.
The servant does not deserve thanks for obeying orders, does he?  It is the same with you, when you have done all you have been told to do, say, we are ordinary servants, we have only done our duty”.
meditation: When the apostles said to the Lord, “make our faith greater”,  Jesus told this parable.  The owner of the property is God. The plowing person or the servant to look after the sheep or the servant from the field is only a servant to obey the orders of the owner.
The servant was appointed to obey and serve the owner at his call. The servant does not deserve any appreciation or thanks from  the owner.
God, the owner, has created all the creation at his will. The human souls or spirits are the ones deputed to the earth as per His plan and they are supposed to obey God as servants.
Servants are to do whatever is commanded by God. It is their bounded duty. No servant can boast about what is entrusted to him.

The servant is not greater than his master. Apostle means, he who was sent as said in John 13:16.  Jesus said that he came from Heaven as he was sent by his Father to do His will only. (as said in John 6:39).

All humans are strangers in the world (1 Peter 2:1). Our souls are provided by God. That is why, Jesus said on Calvary that “Father, In your hands I place my spirit’. Jesus  did and said every word to show as a model for us.

A servant does not know what his master does. Since Jesus revealed all that is said by God to him to his disciples, he wanted not to call servants, but his friends (as said  in John 15:15)  Our hope and faith in Jesus is to live according to his wish, making us eligible to be called as friends by Jesus.
Live according to the wish of God. It is the only way to mankind on earth.
parables.prayer: Our Eternal Father and Creator of the world, give us knowledge and wisdom, to know you and live according to  your wish. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ  Amen.

parables.title: Parable of the Widow and the Judge
scripture: Jesus told his disciples a parable to teach them that they should always pray to God and never become discouraged. “In a certain town there was a judge who never feared God nor respected man. And there was a widow in the same town who kept coming to him and pleading for her rights. ‘help me against my opponent’.

For a very long time the judge refused to act, but at last he said to himself, ‘Even though I don’t fear God or respect man, yet because of all the trouble this widow is giving to me, I will see to it that she gets her rights. If I don’t,  she will keep on coming and finally wear me out’.

And the Lord continued, Listen to what the corrupt judge said. Now, will not God judge in favor of his own people who cry to him day and night for help? Will he be slow to help them? I tell you, he will judge in their favor and do it quickly. But  will the son of Man find faith on earth when he comes?” (Luke 18:1-18).
meditation: In this parable, Jesus emphasized the need of constant and  unstopping  prayers for our genuine and righteous needs of our bodily and spiritual requirements. Because of the human weaknesses, the corrupt judge initially hardened his mind against the widow, he finally decided to provide justice to her since she is constantly begging him to help.

God is not a weak minded person like the corrupt judge. God is not a person to show partiality to some people, like the corrupt judge. Even the corrupt judge himself pitied the widow who is continuously pleading for her rights, God will definitely hear our constant prayers and fulfill them.

Jesus said in Luke 11:13, ‘though bad you are, you know how to give good things to your children. How much more , then,  will the Father in Heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?  The Holy Spirit knows our mind and provides our genuine requirements.

Jesus questioned and searched whether we can find such constantly and faithfully praying persons on earth. Even when people are indulged in worldly attractions and facing temptations, it is very difficult to find people praying constantly with faith and hope, probably they go for worldly solutions.

In the old testament, we will see that Danial, Shedreck, Meshak and Abednego used to pray to God daily and at appointed times. When they were tested by the king, we saw God heard their prayers and saved them and blessed them.

In Luke 11:5-13, we can see a man visiting his friend very very frequently to borrow three loaves of bread to give to his other friend, who is on a journey saying that he is not having any food for him.  His friend says many excuses to avoid help. Yet he will get up and give everything to the asking friend, because he is not ashamed  to keep on asking. Similarly we are to ask our God all our needs and keep faith in God.

When fathers on earth are aware of fulfilling all the needs of their children, our Eternal Father surely provides our spiritual needs.  The Holy Spirit knows our rightful  needs and provides them for the glory of God, at the right time.

After teaching and healing the needy, Jesus used to go to a lonely place and prayed to God. Jesus taught his disciples how to pray to God. Even at the time of crucifixion also Jesus prayed God, “Forgive them, Father, they don’t know what they are doing” in Luke 23:34, and “My God, my God, why do you abandon me” in Mathews 27:46, and also “Father, in your hands,  I place my spirit” in Luke 23:46.

It was written in Acts of the Apostles that the disciples, followers and mother and brothers of Jesus were praying to God constantly. Jesus said in Mathews 7:7, “Ask, and you will receive’. If we pray constantly with faith and hope, God will hear and provide our righteous requests.
God will surely hear those who pray to Him truly and constantly.
parables.prayer: Our heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us the importance of constant prayers. When worldly and corrupt people also change their mind to help the genuine and constant prayers, how can the righteous and loving God leave our prayers unheard?. It is sure and certain that God will provide all our needs in prayers.  Help us to always hold you in our lives.  We pray in the name of Jesus Christ.  Amen.

parables.title: Parable on the prayers of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector
scripture: “Jesus told this parable to people who are sure of their own goodness and despise everybody else. Once there were two men who went up to the temple to pray: one was a pharisee and the other was a tax collector.

The Pharisee stood apart by himself and prayed, ‘I thank you God, that I am not greedy, dishonest, or an adulterer like everybody else. I thank you that I am not like that tax collector over there.  I fast two days a week, and I give a tenth of all my income.

But the Tax collector stood at a distance and would not even raise his face to heaven, but beat on his breast and said, ‘God, pity on me, a sinner.’ ‘I tell you,’  said Jesus, ‘the tax collector, and not the Pharisee, was in the right with God when he went home.
meditation: For every one who makes himself great will be humbled and every one who humbles himself will be made great’.  (Luke 18: 9-14). Which prayer God accepts, is the theme in this parable. Our silent prayer in mind also will reach God, since God knows our mind.

Pharisee felt self-righteous because of his good works like observing fastings and paying tithes regularly and not doing any sin and that he was not like the other gentile person came for praying, and exalted himself, but his prayer revealed his self-righteousness and pride  in his mind. Comparing himself with other persons and exalting himself indicates pride in him.

Jesus said in another parable in Luke 14:7-11, about certain invited people who prefer to select the best place in the wedding feast. when the invited person sits at the lowest place, the host comes and takes him to the best place, it will be an honor for him among the invited persons.

Similarly when an invited person selects a best place and sits there, and when a still more important visitor comes,  the host may ask him to go to a lower place, in order to provide the best place to  the important visitor. It will be a shameful and embarrassing  situation, to go to a lower place leaving the best place.

Therefore Jesus said that everyone who makes himself great will be humbled and everyone who humbles himself will be made great.  While praying in the temple, the pharisee made himself great and his prayer was not accepted by God, while a tax collector humbled himself before God while praying and his prayer was  accepted.  We can see this parable in Luke 18:9-14.

Proverbs 8:13 says, ‘To honor the Lord is to hate  evil, pride and arrogance, evil ways and  false words’. Because of pride, arrogance, and exalting himself, the prayer of the Pharisee was not acceptable to God, though he did many good works.
While the tax collector humbled himself, accepted his sins and prayed for forgiveness, God accepted his prayer and he was treated righteous.
The prayer of those who feel righteous for themselves is boastful, while the prayer with humbleness is acceptable to God.
parables.prayer: Our heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us to be humble before you and that our self-righteousness and pride has no meaning before you.  You are our provider for considering our prayers. Help us to be humble before you and in the right consciousness. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ.  Amen.

parables.title: Parable of the shepherd
scripture: Jesus said, “I am telling you the truth. The man who does not enter the sheepfold by the gate, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber. The man who goes in through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.  The gatekeeper opens the gate for him; the sheep hears his voice as he calls his own sheep by name, and he leads them out.

When he has brought them out he goes ahead of them and the sheep follows him, because they know his voice.  They will not follow someone else; instead, they will run away from such a person, because they do not know his voice”.  (John 10:1-20).

Jesus further said, ‘I am telling you the truth. I am the gate for the sheep. All others who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them. I am the gate. Whoever comes in by me will be saved; he will come in and go out and find pasture. The thief comes only in order to  steal, kill, and destroy.  I have come in order that you might have life   --   life in all its fullness.

“I am the good shepherd, who is willing to die for the sheep. When the hired man who is not a shepherd and does not own the sheep, sees a wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and runs away; so the wolf snatches the sheep and scatters them. The hired man runs away because  he is only a hired man and does not care about the sheep.

I am a good shepherd. As the Father knows me and I know the father, in the same way I know my sheep and they know me. And I am willing to die for them. There are other sheep which belong to me that are not in this sheepfold. I must bring them too, they will listen to my voice, and they will become one folk with one shepherd.

My sheep listen to my voice, I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life and they shall never die. No one can snach them away from me. What my father has given me is greater than everything and no one can snatch them away from the Father’s care. The Father and I are one”.
meditation: In this parable, sheep means the Israelites and the believers. Jesus is the shepherd.  Gate means the truthful way he showed us. Sheepfold is heaven. We have to be thoroughly honest in choosing the righteous way. This parable was said in a very clear way.

Shepherd enters the sheepfold through a gate opened by the gateman. It means Jesus enters the earth in a righteous way and as planned and prophesied in the Law, but not accidentally or by a casual way.

Jesus is the shepherd and the owner. He shows us the right way to follow him. He said, ‘I am the truth, life and the way’. Jesus said that he did everything in a transparent way, no cheating and no doubting anyway, and no shortcuts.

Satan tries to enter into our lives, in a wrong and deceptive way, like the thief enters in a sheepfold not by gate but by jumping in from the fence. We should be faithful, but should not be doubtful or unfaithful. We should be conscious about Satan who tries to create doubts and unfaithfulness.

Jesus loved us first and commanded us to love one another. Jesus faced temptations first in every aspect and showed us a way to overcome temptations. He showed us  the way before us and told us to simply follow him like sheep following the shepherd. We are to keep faith in him and follow.

If we hear him and follow, we get into salvation. It is not enough if we believe, but are supposed to follow. Eternal salvation is God’s will, and the followers get the protection of God and no one can touch them, as said in John 10:27-29. This is our hope.
Jesus is the good shepherd. He saves his followers from trumbles.
parables.prayer: Our heavenly Father, Jesus, the son of God, is our shepherd and he will lead us to heaven. Protect from evil which creates doubts and leads to unfaithfulness. Give us a sheep's mind  to listen to you and follow you honestly. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ.  Amen.

parables.title: Parable of Jesus as the real vine
scripture: “I am the real vine and my Father is the gardener. He breaks off every branch in me that does not bear fruit, and he prunes every branch that does bear fruit, so that it will be clean and bear more fruit. You have been made clean already by the teaching I have given to you.

Remain united in me, and I will remain united to you. A branch cannot bear fruit by itself; it can do so only if it remains in the vine.  In the same way you cannot bear fruit unless you remain in me.

I am the vine and you are the branches. Whoever remains in me and I in him, will bear much fruit;  for you can do nothing without me.  Whoever does not remain in me is thrown out like a branch and dries up; such branches are gathered up and thrown into the fire, where they are burnt.

If you remain in me and my words remain in you, then you will ask for anything you wish, and you shall have it. My Father’s glory is shown by your bearing much fruit; and in this way you become my disciples.”    (John 15:1-8).
meditation: In this parable, Jesus compared himself as vine. Whoever keeps faith in him and lives according to his commandments are compared as branches of him in faith. Branches always remain with the vine, and they only will bear fruits.

If the branches do not remain with the vine, they will be thrown out and dried up. Followers of Jesus are compared as branches. Those followers in Jesus (with his teachings) will be fruitful and will be living models for him, and thereby God is glorified.
Whatever is required and asked by the followers will be provided for the glory of God. Thus the fruitfulness of the followers is explained in this parable.

Luke 12:16-21 says, “There was  once a rich man who had land which bore crops. He began to think for himself. ‘I have nowhere to keep all my crops;. He told himself, ‘I will tear down the barns and build bigger ones, where I will store all my corn and all my other goods.

Then I will say to myself, Lucky man,  you have all the good things you need for many years. Take life easy, eat, drink and enjoy yourself. He secured everything for himself only. But he is not in the living God.  Therefore, if God asks his soul on that night, how can he enjoy his life?
We can be fruitful only when we are attached to God. If not, we get removed and fired as dried stems out of the vine branch.
parables.prayer: Our heavenly Father, we understand that we can be fruitful when we are attached to Jesus and follow. We thank you for the glory given to us to be fruitful, which fruitfulness glorifies God. Protect from evil which makes us not only unfruitful, but also gets thrown out and dried up branches, ultimately getting fired. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ.  Amen.

acknowledgements: “The Word already existed, he was with God, and he was the same as God.” While meditating the Word of God every day in the Bible, I felt an inspiration to list out and meditate on the parables and their meanings  taught by Jesus Christ in the four Gospels, and to make a small effort to place them before the readers.

By following the teachings and commandments of Jesus Christ, we can be fruitful in him with spiritual fruits, live in his truth and righteousness, so that we can be in his love and protection, and God is glorified through our lives.
While meditating on the parables and preparing this small book, I realized a wonderful change in my own attitude, that helped me to be happy, with peace and contentment, and enjoy the Word of God.

I thank God for giving me such inspiration, in the name of Jesus Christ. I am also thankful to many servants of God, who helped me in understanding the word, directly and indirectly, through messages, through Television and other media. Glory to God.  Amen.
